title: The ten sefirot
hookLine: ten emanations through which the Infinite relates to the world
carry: ten lights, one god: the sefirot
last: EIN SOF: THE ONE GOD BEYOND EVERY WORD.

lines: THINE, O LORD, IS THE GREATNESS.
cards: "Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty." King David says it in the book of Chronicles, blessing God in front of the whole assembly.
It sounds like one long sweep of praise. But slow down and count the nouns. In Hebrew each one is its own word, and Jewish mystics read them as more than praise.
To them it was a list: names of the ways the one God shows up in the world. That list has a name of its own.

teach.b: Sefirot. You met the word two days ago in Sefer Yetzirah. In Kabbalah it grows into a whole map: ten lights, or ten emanations, through which Ein Sof, God without end, relates to the world.
First, the number. Sefer Yetzirah insists on it: ten, and not nine; ten, and not eleven. A shape with a definite count.
One common order runs: Keter, crown. Chochmah, wisdom. Binah, understanding.
Chesed, love. Gevurah, strength. Tiferet, beauty.
Netzach, endurance. Hod, splendor. Yesod, foundation.
And Malchut, kingship. Listen for David's verse inside it: gevurah, tiferet, netzach, hod. Kabbalists heard those sefirot in that very line.
Third, the warning. Ten lights does not mean ten gods.

teach.h: A FLAME TIED TO A COAL.
teach.b: Sefer Yetzirah says their end is bound up in their beginning, like a flame tied to a coal.

teach.h: A MAP OF A LIFE, TOO.
teach.b: One fire, many tongues of flame.
Kabbalists say again and again that God is one, and the sefirot are how that one God is turned toward us. Fourth, why it matters on an ordinary afternoon.
The sefirot are also qualities a person has: love, restraint, balance, steadiness, the ability to bring something into the world.
Kabbalists read the human being as built in the same pattern, so the map of how God meets the world doubles as a map of a life.

how: Students of Kabbalah learn the ten sefirot by name and order, often drawn as a diagram, and Hasidic teaching applies them to a person's own character and inner life.

games.q: a friend hears "ten lights" and asks: so there are ten gods? what does the tradition answer?
o: no: one fire, many tongues of flame.
games.why: Sefer Yetzirah says their end is bound to their beginning, like a flame tied to a coal. kabbalists insist God is one.

practice: On each slow breath, say one name quietly with its meaning, from the top down: Keter, crown; Chochmah, wisdom; Binah, understanding; Chesed, love; Gevurah, strength; Tiferet, beauty; Netzach, endurance; Hod, splendor; Yesod, foundation; Malchut, kingship.
Don't worry about getting the order perfect. Let one name catch on something in your own life, and stay with that one.

wordCard.voice: Sefirot. The ten lights, or emanations, through which, in Kabbalah, the one God without end relates to the world, from crown to kingship. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: the sefirot, the ten lights of Kabbalah.

carryVoice: Your line: ten lights, one god: the sefirot. Ten of them, and still one fire with many tongues of flame. Until tomorrow.
